title: Ecma International TC39-relevant MDN issues
description: Issue filed on MDN Web Docs related to pages attached to technologies developed by Ecma International TC39

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Uint32Array

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Start of article

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

Description says:

The Uint32Array typed array represents an array of 32-bit unsigned integers in the platform byte order. If control over byte order is needed, use DataView instead. The contents are initialized to 0 unless initialization data is explicitly provided. Once established, you can reference elements in the array using the object's methods, or using standard array index syntax (that is, using bracket notation).

What did you expect to see?

This may be too obvious but I'd like that the behaviour of passing floats new Uint32Array([1.5,3.2]) is clarified.

Also, if one passes new Uint32Array(new Float32Array([1.5,3.2])) it does the same rounding. But do they share the same buffer in this case, or is there a new buffer created? (I think they don't, but should this be added?)

I think some of this could be added. For example, is 1.5 just floored to 1 by a binary conversion?

What is the expected behaviour when passing a negative number? (seems to be filled with a max value 4294967295)

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

No response

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Thank you MDN 💌

items.content_html:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ReadableStreamDefaultController/close

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Exceptions

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The "Exceptions" section says:

TypeError
Thrown if the source object is not a ReadableStreamDefaultController.

This suggests that errors are not thrown in other cases.

What did you expect to see?

I expect to see that a TypeError may be thrown by this method if the stream is already in the process of closing or closed.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#rs-default-controller-close

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Similar issues exist for ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue and probably methods on WritableStreamDefaultController as well.
